faq.tradingEquities.discoveryBounds.desc: Discovery Bounds are leverage-based limits that restrict how far the price can move from the last official closing price.
faq.tradingEquities.discoveryBounds.rule: The price can only move within a range of 1 / Max Leverage.
faq.tradingEquities.discoveryBounds.bene: This ensures market participants can trade with confidence during the weekend without fear of "flash crashes" or artificial manipulation.
faq.tradingEquities.openInterestCap.stoc: • Popular stocks (e.g., TSLA, NVDA, GOOGL): Caps range from $50M-$100M
faq.tradingEquities.openInterestCap.comm: • Commodities (e.g., GOLD, SILVER, COPPER): Caps range from $100M-$200M
faq.tradingEquities.openInterestCap.fore: • Forex pairs (e.g., EUR, JPY): Caps typically $25M
faq.tradingEquities.openInterestCap.note: These caps are subject to change and will likely increase over time as markets mature. For the most up-to-date OI cap information, visit the asset's detail page in the app.
faq.tradingEquities.fastLiquidation.ques: What happens if the market moves too fast for a liquidation?
faq.tradingEquities.fastLiquidation.answ: In extreme market conditions (like a "black swan" event in a stock), if a trader's position cannot be closed in the open market before their margin runs out, the Insurance Fund steps in to cover the loss. This ensures that no user ever "owes" money to the platform; your maximum loss is always limited to your initial margin.
faq.tradingEquities.autoDeleveraging.que: What is "Auto-Deleveraging" (ADL) and how does it affect me?
faq.tradingEquities.autoDeleveraging.ans: If the Insurance Fund is unable to cover a massive liquidation, the protocol may trigger Auto-Deleveraging. This is a last-resort safety mechanism where the most profitable, highest-leveraged traders on the opposite side of a failing trade have their positions automatically closed at the "Bankruptcy Price."

termsPage.sections.tradingRisksLiquidati: • High-Risk Activity: Leveraged futures trading is highly speculative and can result in total loss of your margin.
• Liquidation Risk: If your perp position's losses exceed your available margin, it will be automatically liquidated.
• Isolated Margin: Only the margin allocated to that specific position is at risk.

• Cross Margin: Under cross margin mode, available margin on your unified trade balance can support eligible perpetual positions. One liquidation event can materially reduce the funds backing your leveraged positions.
• Spot holdings: Buying spot exposes you to market price risk; leveraged perpetual positions may be liquidated when margin becomes insufficient.

• Liquidation and collateral: Leveraged perpetual positions may be liquidated when margin is insufficient. The Interface displays collateral requirements and liquidation prices for your unified trade balance. You are solely responsible for monitoring risk.
• No Advice: Nothing in the App constitutes financial, legal, or tax advice. You are solely responsible for your trading decisions.
